verdict: Across 10 seeds (fresh odour sets + fresh APL->KC shuffles), at density matched to the kWTA baseline (~0.0463), cross-odour cosine (lower = more distinct, mean+-sd over seeds): pure PN->KC drive top-k [0.1, 0.015], uniform APL threshold [0.1074, 0.0141], real per-cell APL->KC [0.13, 0.0158], shuffled APL->KC [0.1794, 0.0156]. The per-cell APL weights do NOT create the odour identity: a structureless uniform threshold is as distinct as the real weights on 90% of seeds, and the pure feedforward top-k (no APL at all) is the MOST distinct on 100% of seeds. The real weights are not random -- shuffling them is worse on 100% of seeds -- but 'beats random' is not 'creates the code': the real-vs-uniform gap (0.0226) is small and within seed spread. This is a DIRECTION supported across seeds, not a proven point estimate. Mechanistically it is near-foreordained: the loop's inhibition is rank<=2 (only 2 APL cell(s)), a near-global modulation that cannot do rich per-cell winner selection. Honest conclusion: the PN->KC wiring gives the odour identity; the APL loop sets only the sparseness level. Settling converged (yes, <= 1.0e-09 residual in <= 63 iters).
